long_biography.plain_text:
Born into Singapore's defining cinema dynasty, Shaw Vee King learned the business from the screen outward. During the 1960s he moved between Singapore and Hong Kong, working across production, distribution and exhibition under his father Runme and uncle Run Run. He also bought films at international festivals and sold Shaw productions abroad.

Returning to Singapore in 1981, Shaw helped reshape a chain challenged by television and video piracy. The group consolidated its local businesses, replaced ageing single-screen venues with multiplexes and redeveloped cinema sites into commercial properties. Away from theatres, he served the Shaw Foundation and led the National Fire Prevention and Civil Emergency Preparedness Council. His civic work brought an Academy of Medicine honorary fellowship and Singapore's Public Service Star.
